explain.narrative:
## try-with-resources and Exception Suppression

try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources automatically, including when the body throws. Resources close in reverse declaration order. If both the body and close operation fail, the body exception remains primary and close failures are suppressed.

## Applying the concept

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that directly supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failure cases and state assumptions clearly.

## Verification checklist

- Compile with JDK 21.
- Predict the output before running.
- Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Check resource cleanup and error handling.
- Prefer explicit types and focused methods.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var in = new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[]{65, 66})) { System.out.println((char) in.read()); } } }
examples.explanation: Uses try-with-resources with an AutoCloseable byte stream.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter()) { writer.write("CodeSaathi"); System.out.println(writer.toString()); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows automatic resource closure for a writer.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class R implements AutoCloseable { public void close() { System.out.println("closed"); } } try (R r = new R()) { System.out.println("body"); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows that close runs after the try body.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class R implements AutoCloseable { public void close() throws Exception { throw new Exception("close"); } } try (R r = new R()) { throw new Exception("body"); } catch (Exception ex) { System.out.println(ex.getMessage()); System.out.println(ex.getSuppressed()[0].getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows that a body exception remains primary and a close failure is suppressed.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var one = new java.io.StringReader("one"); var two = new java.io.StringReader("two")) { System.out.println((char) one.read() + (char) two.read()); } } }
examples.explanation: Declares multiple resources; they close automatically in reverse order.
